Leukemia.title: Nosology and classification
Leukemia.text: Leukemia is a cancer of the blood cells. It usually begins in the bone marrow where blood cells are formed.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Diagnostic tests
Leukemia.text: Your doctor can request lab analyses for leukemia that include blood tests that check the levels and types of blood cells and look for changes in the shape of blood cells.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Symptoms and clinical findings
Leukemia.text: During the early stages of leukemia, there may be no symptoms. Many of the symptoms of leukemia don't become apparent until a large number of normal blood cells are crowded out by leukemia cells.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Mechanism and pathophysiology
Leukemia.text: Over time, as the number of abnormal white blood cells builds up in the blood, they crowd out healthy blood cells.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Nosology and classification
Leukemia.text: There are four common types of leukemia. They are chronic lymphocytic leukemia, chronic myeloid leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, and acute lymphocytic leukemia.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Epidemiology and etiology
Leukemia.text: For the most part, no one knows why some people develop leukemia and others do not. Most people who have known risk factors do not get leukemia, while many who get the disease do not have any risk factors.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Symptoms and clinical findings
Leukemia.text: Common symptoms of leukemia may include - fevers - frequent infections - feeling weak or tired - headache - bleeding and bruising easily - pain in the bones or joints - swelling or discomfort in the abdomen (from an enlarged spleen) - swollen lymph nodes, especially in the neck or armpit - weight loss.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Therapeutic classes
Leukemia.text: Treatment depends on a number of factors, including the type of leukemia, the patient's age and general health, where leukemia cells have collected in the body, and whether the leukemia has been treated before.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Therapeutic classes
Leukemia.text: Chemotherapy is a cancer treatment that uses drugs to kill cancer cells.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.text: Clinical trials test an intervention such as a drug, therapy, medical device, or behavior in many people to see if it is safe and effective.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Trials and evidence
Leukemia.text: Clinical trials often compare a new treatment with a standard treatment to determine which one gives better results.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.text: There is no standard staging system for adult AML.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Diagnostic tests
Leukemia.text: Cytogenetic analysis : A laboratory test in which the cells in a sample of blood or bone marrow are viewed under a microscope to look for certain changes in the chromosomes. Other tests, such as fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), may also be done to look for certain changes in the chromosomes.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Leukemia.title: Diagnostic tests
Leukemia.text: Immunophenotyping : A process used to identify cells, based on the types of antigens or markers on the surface of the cell. This process is used to diagnose the subtype of AML by comparing the cancer cells to normal cells of the immune system.
Leukemia.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Lung Cancer.text: Lung cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the lung.
Lung Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Lung Cancer.text: Most cases of lung cancer are not related to inherited gene changes. These cancers are associated with somatic mutations that occur only in certain cells in the lung.
Lung Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Lung Cancer.title: Symptoms and clinical findings
Lung Cancer.text: When lung cancer first develops, there may be no symptoms at all.
Lung Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Osteoporosis.title: Nosology and classification
Osteoporosis.text: Osteoporosis makes your bones weak and more likely to break. Anyone can develop osteoporosis, but it is common in older women.
Osteoporosis.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Parkinson's Disease.title: Nosology and classification
Parkinson's Disease.text: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a type of movement disorder. It happens when nerve cells in the brain don't produce enough of a brain chemical called dopamine.
Parkinson's Disease.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Parkinson's Disease.title: Epidemiology and etiology
Parkinson's Disease.text: Most cases of Parkinson disease occur in people with no apparent family history of the disorder. These sporadic cases may not be inherited, or they may have an inheritance pattern that is unknown.
Parkinson's Disease.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Parkinson's Disease.text: Many Parkinson disease symptoms occur when nerve cells (neurons) in the substantia nigra die or become impaired.
Parkinson's Disease.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Parkinson's Disease.text: Lewy bodies are unusual deposits or clumps of the brain protein alpha-synuclein, along with other proteins, which are seen upon microscopic examination of the brain.
Parkinson's Disease.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Prostate Cancer.text: Prostate cancer is a disease in which malignant (cancer) cells form in the tissues of the prostate.
Prostate Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Prostate Cancer.text: Signs of prostate cancer include a weak flow of urine or frequent urination. These and other signs and symptoms may be caused by prostate cancer or by other conditions.
Prostate Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Prostate Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Psoriasis.title: Nosology and classification
Psoriasis.text: Psoriasis is a skin disease that causes itchy or sore patches of thick, red skin with silvery scales. You usually get the patches on your elbows, knees, scalp, back, face, palms and feet, but they can show up on other parts of your body.
Psoriasis.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.
Psoriasis.vintage: Historical MedQuAD excerpt. Repository snapshot 2023-10-17; source publication date unverified.

Psoriasis.title: Diagnostic tests
Psoriasis.text: In most cases, your primary care doctor can diagnose psoriasis simply by examining your skin.
Psoriasis.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.
Psoriasis.vintage: Historical MedQuAD excerpt. Repository snapshot 2023-10-17; source publication date unverified.

Psoriasis.title: Symptoms and clinical findings
Psoriasis.text: Different forms of psoriasis have different symptoms. In many cases your doctor can diagnose psoriasis based on the signs seen in the physical exam as well as the symptoms you describe.
Psoriasis.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Psoriasis.title: Mechanism and pathophysiology
Psoriasis.text: The body does not shed these excess cells and they build up on the surface of the skin, forming thick, scaly patches.
Psoriasis.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Shingles.title: Nosology and classification
Shingles.text: Shingles is a disease caused by the varicella-zoster virus - the same virus that causes chickenpox. After you have chickenpox, the virus stays in your body.
Shingles.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.
Shingles.vintage: Historical MedQuAD excerpt. Repository snapshot 2023-10-17; source publication date unverified.

Shingles.title: Risk and prognosis
Shingles.text: The leading risk factor for shingles is a history of having had chickenpox.
Shingles.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.
Shingles.vintage: Historical MedQuAD excerpt. Repository snapshot 2023-10-17; source publication date unverified.

Shingles.title: Symptoms and clinical findings
Shingles.text: An outbreak of shingles usually begins with a burning, itching, or tingling sensation on the back, chest, or around the rib cage or waist. It is also common for the face or eye area to be affected.
Shingles.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.
Shingles.vintage: Historical MedQuAD excerpt. Repository snapshot 2023-10-17; source publication date unverified.

Shingles.title: Risk and prognosis
Shingles.text: Conditions that weaken the immune system can also put people at risk for shingles.
Shingles.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.
Shingles.vintage: Historical MedQuAD excerpt. Repository snapshot 2023-10-17; source publication date unverified.

Shingles.title: Mechanism and pathophysiology
Shingles.text: The virus travels from the spinal nerve cells and follows a nerve path out to the skin.
Shingles.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Skin Cancer.text: Skin cancer occurs when cancer cells form in the tissues of the skin.
Skin Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Skin Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Skin Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Skin Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Skin Cancer.text: Skin cancer occurs when abnormal cells form and multiply in an uncontrolled way in the epidermis, or abnormal cells from the epidermis invade the dermis of the skin.
Skin Cancer.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Stroke.text: A stroke occurs when the blood supply to part of the brain is suddenly interrupted or when a blood vessel in the brain bursts, spilling blood into the spaces surrounding brain cells.
Stroke.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Stroke.text: Your doctor will diagnose a stroke based on your signs and symptoms, your medical history, a physical exam, and test results.
Stroke.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Stroke.text: Certain traits, conditions, and habits can raise your risk of having a stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). These traits, conditions, and habits are known as risk factors.
Stroke.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Stroke.text: The signs and symptoms of a stroke often develop quickly.
Stroke.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Stroke.text: An ischemic stroke is caused by a blood clot that blocks or plugs a blood vessel supplying blood to the brain.
Stroke.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Stroke.text: Sudden bleeding in the brain also can cause a stroke if it damages brain cells.
Stroke.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.

Stroke.title: Risk and prognosis
Stroke.text: A stroke can cause lasting brain damage, long-term disability, or even death.
Stroke.attribution: MedQuAD, Asma Ben Abacha and Dina Demner-Fushman (2019), A Question-Entailment Approach to Question Answering, doi:10.1186/s12859-019-3119-4. Excerpt selected and whitespace normalized.
